summary: A 1976 discussion of the RCTE Telnet option, collected as a dialogue following the publication of RFC 718. It raises points on how the option is negotiated and on clearing input buffers.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 719 records implementers' discussion following the RCTE option specification. They consider how peers negotiate the mode and how a synch-datamark can clear input and reset counters.

subtitle: Implementer comments on negotiating and using the RCTE Telnet option.

tldr.problem: Implementers discussing the RCTE Telnet option raised questions about negotiation and how to clear input while the option is active.

today: RFC 719 is a discussion of implementer comments on RCTE following RFC 718. Its final note says a revised RCTE specification would be prepared.

sections.title: Questions About RCTE
sections.content:
The memo reproduces significant parts of a dialogue that followed RFC 718. Participants discuss the negotiation sequence for RCTE and a need to clear the input buffer while the option is active.

The document is a record of comments exchanged by implementers, not a standalone RCTE protocol specification.
sections.plainLanguage: Implementers tried to clarify how the RCTE option should be enabled. They also wanted a defined way to clear buffered input.

sections.title: Negotiating the Mode
sections.content:
One participant says the normal exchange is for the server to send “WILL RCTE” and the user to send “DO RCTE.” The discussion also says the response to a server's “DO RCTE” should be made explicit and can serve as the synchronization mark for the change.

The messages in the discussion describe a proposal for clarifying the negotiation, rather than a normative revised specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The peers need to agree before using RCTE. The discussion identifies the reply as the point that marks the mode change.

sections.title: Clearing Input and Option Interactions
sections.content:
The participants propose using a synch-datamark to clear the input buffer and reset counters while synchronizing the action. They discuss treating Abort Output as a request for the other side to send that mark when RCTE is active.

They also discuss interactions with other options: suppressing GO-AHEAD while using RCTE, restoring the previous ECHO mode when leaving it, and not combining RCTE with BINARY.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposed clear operation uses a synchronized data mark and resets counters. The discussion also identifies other Telnet settings that would need compatible behavior.
